**Position Summary:**  
The Lead Clinical Research Coordinator, **located at our site in Pomona, California**, is responsible for managing and coordinating the day-to-day operations of clinical research studies, while also providing  
site-level leadership, mentorship, and oversight to the coordinator team. Reporting to the Site Manager, the Lead CRC ensures protocol compliance, data integrity, and inspection readiness, and serves as the primary resource and first point of escalation for the coordinator group.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Coordinate and manage clinical research protocols from start-up to close-out.
* Recruit, screen, consent, and enroll eligible participants in compliance with study protocols and ethical guidelines.
* Collect, record, and maintain accurate data and source documentation for each study subject.
* Schedule and conduct study visits and procedures per protocol and ICH-GCP standards.
* Prepare and submit IRB submissions, amendments, continuing reviews, and adverse event reports.
* Ensure timely and accurate data entry into electronic data capture (EDC) systems.
* Serve as the primary point of contact for sponsors, CROs, monitors, and regulatory bodies.
* Maintain and organize regulatory binders and study documentation in compliance with FDA and GCP requirements.
* Monitor study inventory and order supplies as needed.
* Support audit readiness and participate in monitoring visits, audits, and inspections.
* Educate and communicate with study participants regarding study procedures, risks, and responsibilities.
* Attend study training, site initiation visits (SIVs), and investigator meetings as needed.

**Leadership Responsibilities:**

* Serve as the primary site-level resource and mentor for clinical research coordinators, including onboarding and ongoing training of new staff.
* Oversee distribution of study assignments and monitor team workload, visit coverage, and protocol timelines across coordinators.
* Conduct quality review of case report forms and source documentation completed by other coordinators to support data integrity and inspection readiness.
* Serve as the first point of escalation for protocol questions, monitor findings, and routine sponsor and IRB communications, escalating to the Site Manager as needed.
* Support the Site Manager with operational coordination, scheduling, and site readiness, and provide coverage in the Site Manager's absence where appropriate.
* Maintain site-level training documentation and support team-wide GCP and regulatory compliance.

**Qualifications**  
**Education:**

* Bachelor’s degree in health sciences, life sciences, nursing, or related field required.
* Certification as a Clinical Research Coordinator (CCRC) or equivalent preferred.

**Experience:**

* Minimum 3-4 years of experience in clinical research, preferably in a coordinator role, with demonstrated progression in scope and responsibility.
* Experience with IRB processes, electronic data capture (e.g., REDCap, Medidata), and GCP compliance.
* Prior experience mentoring, coaching, or leading coordinator-level staff strongly preferred.

**Skills:**

* Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
* Ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook).
* Familiarity with HIPAA and human subject protection regulations.

**Working Conditions:**

* May involve direct patient interaction, phlebotomy, specimen processing, and travel between sites.
* Must be able to work occasional evenings or weekends depending on study requirements.

**Physical Requirements:**

* Ability to stand, walk, sit, use hands, and reach with arms.
* Ability to lift up to 25 pounds occasionally.

**Pay:**

$85-95k, dependent on experience

Job Summary:

**Job Summary**

We are seeking a highly organized and proactive professional to serve as Executive Assistant to the John E. and Louise Bryson Director of the Getty Conservation Institute. This position oversees day-to-day operations for the director’s office and provides high-level administrative and operational support. The Executive Assistant is key in managing priorities and communications, coordinating activities, and ensuring the efficient functioning of the office in support of the Director’s priorities and the Institute’s mission.

**About Us**

The Getty Conservation Institute is dedicated to finding ways to improve conservation of the world’s cultural heritage—its art objects, museum collections, historic buildings, and archaeological sites and our work often takes place at heritage sites across the globe including locations in South America, Asia, and the Middle East, where we work in partnership with heritage professionals from the region. Our staff have expertise in architecture, archaeology, conservation, engineering, chemistry, materials science, physics, information science, operations management, administration, and communications.

This job will be based in our office at the Getty Center in Los Angeles. It will begin in the office full-time and the opportunity to request a telework schedule may be available after an initial period of training and orientation and will be discussed and approved by your supervisor. Typically, staff with approved telework schedules at the Getty Conservation Institute are in the office more than half of the time.

Major Job Responsibilities:

As the Executive Assistant, you will:

* Proactively manage the director’s attention and focus by anticipating needs, clarifying priorities, and ensuring that the director’s time is directed to the most important issues.
* Manage a complex executive calendar, involving competing requests and multiple scheduling priorities.
* Track inquiries received by the director via email, phone, and mail to ensure timely responses; and maintain director’s database of colleagues’ contact information.
* Coordinate all aspects of the director’s national and international business travel arrangements, which also includes preparation of briefing materials and background information for meetings and trips, and timely completion of expense reports in compliance with Getty policies.
* Maintain the director’s office records in accordance with institutional records management policies. This work regularly involves records of enduring value that document the organization's history and requires preservation of such materials and Getty intellectual property.
* Organize internal and external events of various sizes, which may include venue, catering, technology, and audio-visual arrangements.
* Develop agendas, notes, minutes, and other communications on behalf of the director, including drafting and proofreading correspondence, reports, publications, and presentations, including light editing of images.
* Gather, evaluate, and synthesize information from multiple sources to develop written briefing materials for the director, as requested.
* Process contracts and payments, prepare and track the director’s office budget, procure supplies, implement special projects requested by the director, and perform other duties as assigned.
* Represent the Getty Conservation Institute and the director’s office with professionalism, discretion, and sound judgment in interactions inside and outside Getty.
* Serve as a trusted ambassador who is capable of safeguarding and strengthening key relationships with peers, senior leaders, trustees, donors, and partners.

In all aspects of your responsibilities, you will work under the general direction of the director while exercising independence and sound judgment on the director’s behalf to address complex, sensitive, or ambiguous issues and make decisions in a fast-paced environment.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 7 years of related experience, including experience providing executive-level support

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

* Ability to thrive and remain composed in a fast-paced work environment.
* Able to recognize when to act independently and when to consult the director.
* Excellent problem-solving, capable of resolving complex issues or identifying well-considered solutions for the director.
* Strategic prioritization and exemplary judgment. Able to understand the office’s priorities and make sound decisions about where the director’s attention is needed.
* Proactive in identifying the director’s needs and external challenges before they become pressing.
* Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Effective communications skills, both written and verbal; ability to proofread.
* High level of discretion.
* Demonstrated success in planning, organizing and completing projects.
* Self-motivated, able to anticipate emerging tasks.
* Able to balance your own workload between shifting demands and routine office operations.
* Advanced computer skills; able to effectively use technology to access, manage, synthesize, and communicate information. Must be proficient in Microsoft Office applications (including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint and OneDrive); familiarity with Blackbaud Raiser’s Edge, and photo editing software

* Experience in automotive, retail, or other consumer-facing commercial operations preferred
* Experience owning KPI frameworks and governing metric definitions across complex, multi-stakeholder organizations
* Demonstrated ability to assess performance at site, regional, and portfolio levels — and connect macro trends to micro-level outcomes across a distributed organization
* Fluency in data visualization tools such as Tableau, Hex, or similar, with experience shaping dashboard design and working directly with analytics or data engineering teams
* Familiarity with Salesforce or similar CRM operations and analytics tooling preferred

**Job Description**

**CUSTOMS AND LOGISTICS COORDINATOR**

**Summary:** Customs and Logistics Coordinator provides support to imports/exports Customs clearance and compliance, domestic/international freight bookings and third-party warehouse day-to-day operations. This role requires familiarity with national and international trade regulations, as well as the ability to successfully categorize and classify shipments based on a complex tariff coding system.

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

Customs and Logistics Coordinator is responsible for the following activities:

* Coordinate paperwork flow between Company and Customs brokers.
* Prepare and file Customs Forms as needed.
* Work with Customs brokers on classifying and assigning HST# to new products.
* Maintaining HST# updated in the system.
* Assure compliance with Customs regulations.
* Handling Customs inquiries and audits.
* Coordinate transportation providers to ensure prompt and proper movement of shipments.
* Review purchase orders/invoices and shipping documents to ensure accuracy.
* Make special shipping arrangements as necessary.
* Track and fix shipping errors.
* Maintain relationship with third-party warehouse.
* Organize daily domestic/international shipment plans.
* Manage day-to-day operations and flows with third-party warehouse (items, EAN codes, serial #, picking lists, picking lists confirmations, packing lists, tracking# confirmations, etc.).
* Monitor KPIs.
* Define and manage freight and warehousing budgets.
* Ensure that the quality of all services provided meets the required standard.
* Develop processes that make the supply chain more efficient and organized.

**Requirements:**

Customs and Logistics Coordinator uses a variety of soft skills and industry knowledge of best practices to maintain and improve the stages of the supply chain. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required:

* Strong working knowledge of US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) requirements.
* Experience with US ACE interface.
* Understanding of 19 CFR (Parts 1 – 199) and the US HTS.
* Knowledge of Canadian customs import regulations.
* Effective communication, including writing, speaking and interpersonal communication.
* Quick critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
* Excellent customer service and client relations skills.
* Keep organization and time management skills.
* Good collaboration and teamwork abilities.
* Great leadership and goal-setting skills.
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment.
* Advanced data analysis and data visualization.
* Expert inventory management.
* Ability to use computers, software and other technology for inventory and communication purposes.
* Understanding of the supply chain, including common obstacles and effective solutions.
* International and national trade-related knowledge.

**Education:**

Associate or a bachelor’s degree in a related field, such as business, supply chain management or a related field.

**Language Ability:**

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret general business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations. Ability to write reports, business correspondence, and procedure manuals. Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers, and the general public.

**Physical Demands:**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

new_jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced **Project Coordinator III** to support financial operations, spend governance, budgeting, forecasting, and process optimization within a leading technology company's hardware engineering organization.

This highly visible role partners directly with engineering leaders, finance stakeholders, procurement teams, and senior management to manage budgets, analyze spending trends, develop actionable financial insights, and improve operational efficiency.

The ideal candidate brings a strong foundation in financial operations and data analytics, combined with excellent stakeholder communication skills and practical experience leveraging AI and automation to streamline business processes.

**This is not a traditional administrative project coordination position.** The role combines hands-on financial analysis and reporting with process improvement, change management, and AI driven workflow optimization.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

**Financial Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting**

* Support annual and quarterly budgeting and forecasting cycles for engineering and hardware development teams.
* Track operating expenditures (OpEx), capital expenditures (CapEx), budget commitments, and actual spending against forecasts.
* Analyze financial data, identify spending variances, and provide actionable insights and recommendations to leadership.
* Audit budget submissions, validate data accuracy, and identify financial risks and opportunities.
* Coordinate monthly accrual processes, including validating purchase orders, outstanding commitments, and received goods or services.

**Reporting, Analytics & Executive Communication**

* Develop and maintain weekly and monthly financial reports, dashboards, and spending summaries.
* Build financial models and reporting tools using advanced Excel or Google Sheets functionality.
* Create data visualizations and executive dashboards using Tableau, Power BI, Looker, or comparable BI platforms.
* Translate complex financial data into clear recommendations for directors and senior stakeholders.
* Collaborate with budget owners to identify spending challenges, resolve discrepancies, and improve resource allocation.

**AI Automation & Process Improvement**

* Identify opportunities to streamline budgeting, reporting, and financial operations through AI and automation.
* Develop reusable AI agents, assistants, prompts, and automated workflows to improve efficiency and reporting accuracy.
* Support the implementation of new processes, tools, and operational improvements.
* Partner with cross-functional teams to drive adoption of new workflows and scalable solutions.
* Apply analytical thinking to improve existing business processes and reduce manual effort.

**Cross Functional Collaboration & Project Coordination**

* Serve as a trusted resource for engineering leaders and budget owners regarding spending, forecasts, and financial processes.
* Partner with Procurement, Sourcing, Accounts Payable, and Program Management teams.
* Track action items, coordinate follow-ups, and ensure timely resolution of outstanding issues.
* Support stakeholders through complex planning cycles while maintaining accuracy and meeting critical deadlines.

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* **5+ years of professional experience** in financial operations, spend tracking, budgeting, forecasting, or resource and capacity analysis.
* Strong hands-on experience analyzing financial data and developing financial reports for business stakeholders.
* Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills, including complex formulas, pivot tables, lookups, and financial modeling.
* Experience developing dashboards and visualizations using Tableau, Power BI, Looker, or similar business intelligence tools.
* Practical experience with **prompt engineering, AI agents, or workflow automation tools** to improve business processes.
* Demonstrated ability to prepare and present financial analysis, findings, and recommendations to directors or senior leadership.
* Strong analytical skills with the ability to identify trends, investigate financial discrepancies, and recommend improvements.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, organizational skills, and attention to detail.
* Ability to work independently, manage ambiguity, and proactively drive deliverables to completion.
* Experience handling confidential financial, vendor, and resource information.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Engineering, Business Analytics, Data Science, Statistics, or a related quantitative field.
* Financial operations or spend governance experience supporting engineering, hardware, research and development, or manufacturing organizations.
* Exposure to consumer electronics development and New Product Introduction (NPI) processes.
* Experience working within large technology or consumer hardware organizations.
* Experience implementing new operational processes, workflow improvements, or change management initiatives.
* Professional certifications in data analytics, business intelligence, SQL, or related disciplines.

**Why This Opportunity?**
-------------------------

This opportunity offers direct exposure to engineering directors and senior leadership within a major technology organization. You will have the opportunity to influence financial decisions, optimize spending across hardware development initiatives, and help shape how AI and automation are integrated into critical business operations.

The role offers a unique blend of **financial analytics, strategic stakeholder engagement, and emerging AI technologies**, making it an excellent opportunity for professionals who enjoy working with data while driving meaningful operational improvements.

**Role type:** Contract 2 months (strong possibility for extension)

**Expected hours**: 40 per week

**About Ramp**
==============

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* Build account strategies using company context, growth signals, financial workflows, and stakeholder priorities.
* Research and engage finance leaders through personalized phone, email, and multi-channel outreach.
* Qualify prospects through consultative discovery, connecting workflow challenges to business impact.
* Clearly explain how Ramp can help finance teams simplify spend management, reduce manual work, and gain visibility and control across financial operations.
* Handle objections with sound judgment and earn the right to a next conversation.
* Partner with Account Executives on account planning, sequencing, and opportunity creation.
* Use AI and other tools thoughtfully to strengthen research, prioritization, personalization, and workflow efficiency; validate outputs before using them.

* Strong written and verbal communication: concise, customer-focused, and specific.
* Strong discovery and objection-handling fundamentals.
* Commercial judgment: form a point of view, explain tradeoffs, and adapt based on new information.
* A builder mindset: identify improvements, create repeatable systems, and learn from results.
* Practical AI fluency and sound judgment using tools to improve quality and speed.

OpenGov is the leader in AI and ERP solutions for local and state governments in the U.S. More than 2,000 cities, counties, state agencies, school districts, and special districts rely on the OpenGov Public Service Platform to operate efficiently, adapt to change, and strengthen the public trust. Category-leading products include enterprise asset management, procurement and contract management, accounting and budgeting, billing and revenue management, permitting and licensing, and transparency and open data. These solutions come together in the OpenGov ERP, allowing public sector organizations to focus on priorities and deliver maximum ROI with every dollar and decision in sync. Learn about OpenGov’s mission to power more effective and accountable government and the vision of high-performance government for every community at OpenGov.com.

**Job Summary:**
----------------

The Sales Development Representative (SDR) is the front line of OpenGov's mission. You won't just be generating pipeline — you'll be connecting government leaders with technology that helps their communities run better. This role is built for people who are hungry to grow, competitive by nature, and motivated by the idea that their work genuinely matters. You'll receive hands-on training, real mentorship, and a clear path into a full-cycle sales career — all at a company where the mission is worth showing up for.

**Responsibilities:**
---------------------

* Build and own your pipeline — research market trends and identify fresh business opportunities for OpenGov within your assigned territory through high-volume outbound calls, emails, and LinkedIn outreach
* Become the expert — get deep on OpenGov's cloud-based platform so you can speak fluently about the real problems it solves for cities, counties, special districts, and state agencies
* Partner with Account Executives — develop territory strategy together, qualify opportunities that lead to demos, and collaborate on approaches that convert prospects into customers
* Work the tools — use Salesforce, Outreach, and LinkedIn to generate daily activity, prioritize leads, and manage your pipeline with precision
* Communicate with impact — clearly and persuasively articulate OpenGov's value and quickly establish credibility with government decision-makers
* Stay high-volume and high-quality — maintain strong prospecting activity each week while staying adaptable, focused, and coachable
* Show up in the field — attend trade shows and government events, promote OpenGov's offerings, and build real relationships with the people running our cities
* Follow through on leads — analyze and follow up with conference and event leads to convert every opportunity worth pursuing
* Collaborate with marketing — work cross-functionally to ensure strong lead-to-opportunity conversion from campaigns and inbound activity

**What Sets Our SDR Team Apart:**
---------------------------------

* A clear path to Account Executive. SDRs who hit quota consistently and take ownership of their development are promoted to AE. You'll have a structured ramp, real mentorship from senior AEs, and a playbook built around your success.
* Spiffs that actually motivate. We run regular performance competitions throughout the year with real stakes — our most recent top performers earned tickets to the 2026 World Cup. The leaderboard is always live.
* The mission is real. OpenGov serves 2,000+ governments. The deals you help close become better tools for the people running our cities, counties, and communities.

**Requirements and Preferred Experience:**
------------------------------------------

* 0–2 years of experience in sales, a customer-facing role, or anything that sharpened your communication — internships, campus jobs, retail, service industry, and bootcamps all count
* A natural communicator who's confident talking to people you've never met — and knows how to make them glad you called
* Genuinely curious about technology and its role in government, with a competitive drive and real passion for pushing the public sector forward
* Excited by AI and what it means for government — OpenGov is at the forefront of bringing AI into public sector operations, and we want SDRs who geek out on that, can speak to it credibly, and see it as the reason this is one of the most interesting sales opportunities in the market right now
* Bachelor's degree preferred
* Familiarity with CRM tools (Salesforce or similar) is a plus
* Background in B2B, SaaS, finance, budgeting, or government is a bonus — but not expected at this level

**Compensation:**
-----------------

San Francisco, CA: $65,000 – $75,000

On target ranges above include base plus a portion of variable compensation that is earned based on company and individual performance.

The final compensation will be determined by a number of factors such as qualifications, expertise, and the candidate’s geographical location.

**Why OpenGov?**
================

**A Mission That Matters.**

At OpenGov, public service is personal. We are passionate about our mission to power more effective and accountable government. Government that operates efficiently, adapts to change, and strengthens public trust. Some people say this is boring. We think it’s the core of our democracy.

**Opportunity to Innovate**

The next great wave of innovation is unfolding with AI, and it will impact everything—from the way we work to the way governments interact with their residents. Join a trusted team with the passion, technology, and expertise to drive innovation and bring AI to local government. We’ve touched 2,000 communities so far, and we’re just getting started.

**A Team of Passionate, Driven People**

This isn’t your typical 9-to-5 job; we operate in a fast-paced, results-driven environment where impact matters more than simply clocking in and out. Our global team of 800+ employees is united in our commitment to challenge the status quo. OpenGov is headquartered in San Francisc

new_jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

North America Seller Business (NASB) Finance Team is seeking a Finance Manager to serve as the strategic finance partner for Strategic Account Services (SAS) and New Seller Recruitment (NSR) businesses. In this role, you will own end-to-end P&L management, deliver financial insights that drive business decisions, and partner closely with senior business leaders to optimize performance and accelerate growth. You will play a critical role in shaping the financial strategy for programs that directly impact Amazon's third-party seller ecosystem, from recruiting new sellers to scaling the success of established ones.  
  
The ideal candidate is a self-starter who thrives in ambiguity, can translate complex financial data into actionable narratives, and is passionate about influencing business outcomes through financial partnership.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Own end-to-end P&L management for SAS and NSR, including forecasting, variance analysis, and financial reporting,
* Serve as the primary finance partner to SAS and NSR business leaders (Directors), providing strategic guidance on P&L management, investment decisions, headcount planning, and resource allocation,
* Lead Monthly Financial Reviews (MFRs) and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), delivering clear visibility into performance drivers and key input metrics (selection, pricing, inventory...),
* Develop and maintain financial models to evaluate business proposals, program ROI, and scenario analyses,
* Identify and communicate risks and opportunities through deep-dive analysis, and recommend actionable mitigation strategies,
* Partner cross-functionally with New Seller Recruitment Team, Strategic Account Services Team , Business Intelligence teams to ensure data accuracy and alignment on planning assumptions,
* Support goal-setting frameworks and reporting processes,
* Develop and automate reporting mechanisms to improve efficiency and scalability of financial processes,
* Champion AI-driven innovation by designing and deploying AI agents and knowledge bases for SAS and NSR that scale business operations and automate workflows,
* Influence business strategy by providing data-driven insights on seller economics, fee structures, and program effectiveness.

  
A day in the life  
Your morning might start with reviewing the latest seller performance and identifying trends in SAS seller attribution or NSR recruitment metrics. By mid-morning, you're in a working session with the NSR program lead, aligning on goal-setting assumptions and refining the financial model for an upcoming business review.  
  
After lunch, you join a cross-functional meeting with the SAS program team to walk through variance drivers from the latest MFR, explaining how seller enrollments, headcount changes, or program investments are impacting the P&L. You provide clear, concise narratives that help leadership understand the "so what" behind the numbers.  
  
Later in the afternoon, you're building a scenario analysis for a new seller incentive proposal, stress-testing assumptions and quantifying the expected ROI. Before wrapping up, you connect with your finance peers to align on planning inputs for the upcoming OP2 cycle.  
  
No two days are exactly alike, but every day involves a blend of analytical deep-dives, strategic partnership, and storytelling through data.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* 5+ years of applying key financial performance indicators (KPIs) to analyses experience
* 5+ years of building financial and operational reports/data sets that inform business decision-making experience
* 5+ years of participating in continuous improvement projects in your team to scale and improve controllership with measurable results experience
* 5+ years of finance, accounting, or related analytical field experience
* Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting or related field

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* 5+ years of solving complex business challenges by delivering accurate and timely financial models, analysis, and recommendations that have a proven impact on business (e.g., financial savings, operational improvements, or customer benefits) experience
* Knowledge of SQL/ETL
* Experience working with large-scale data mining and reporting tools (examples: SQL, MS Access, Essbase, Cognos) and other financial systems (examples: Oracle, SAP, Lawson, JD Edwards)
* Experience delivering forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis, and data interpretation of results

Within our Construction & Design vertical, we have a team that specializes in providing insurance brokerage and risk consulting services for construction and design professionals, specifically large accounts for architect & engineering firms (A/E). What differentiates us is our construction industry expertise. Our leaders have prior experience as practicing construction lawyers (in-house and outside), engineers, consultants, and underwriters – giving us a unique and unmatched insight into how A/E firms operate, deliver projects, and manage risks. **LOCATION:** Hybrid required, 3 days a week in-office - in Alpharetta GA, Chicago IL, or St. Louis MO.

* High attention to detail, and the ability to learn and understand software systems quickly.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO:**

Pindrop is a cybersecurity company delivering continuous identity verification across voice, video, and digital interactions. Powered by the Pindrop Intelligence Network, our unified trust platform helps enterprises answer three critical questions:

**Is this identity risky?** Identify fraud, suspicious behavior, and other risk signals.

* Use AI and modern productivity tools to streamline workflows, summarize materials, and enhance decision-making.

Confidentiality and trust

* Handle sensitive information with discretion and professionalism.
* Build trusted relationships across all levels of the organization and maintain confidentiality at all times.

**Who you are**
---------------

* A polished, composed executive partner with strong taste, sound judgment, and the confidence to hold and share a point of view.

We have grown very quickly since our founding, and we continue to see growth and success thanks to our hard-working and growth-minded employees.

Our core values are: Owner mindset, Inspire trust, Think big, and Drive results. If these values and growth align with what you're looking for in your next career? Then consider joining our amazing team!

Within our Construction & Design vertical, we have a team that specializes in providing insurance brokerage and risk consulting services for construction and design professionals, specifically large accounts for architect & engineering firms (A/E). **LOCATION:** Hybrid required, 3 days a week in-office - in Alpharetta GA, Chicago IL, or St. Louis MO.

* High attention to detail, and the ability to learn and understand software systems quickly.
* **REQUIRED: At least 5+ years** of experience working for an insurance agency, broker or carrier, **AND experience working with Controlled Insurance Programs (OCIPs, CCIPs) and Builder's Risk**
* Candidates who adapt well to priority changes, deadlines, and who love problem solving and coming up with solutions and answers to client questions.

  

**WHAT YOU'LL DO:**

A detailed list of job duties includes (but is not limited to):

Critical Job Functions:  
The account manager will handle day-to-day client issues and questions, including but not limited to:  

* Answer client questions and resolve client problems

Proactively manage the insurance renewal and new business process in accordance with EPIC's timing standards.

Job Accountability Measures:

**WHAT YOU'LL BRING:**

**Render Goods | Chicago, IL | $22/hour**

**Monday–Friday | Starting 20 Hours per Week | Flexible Scheduling**

About the Role:

Render Goods is looking for a reliable, organized, and hands-on person to help with the day-to-day operations of our Chicago housewares studio.

This is a part-time, in-person position working directly alongside me, the founder, to keep orders moving, products looking their best, and daily studio operations running smoothly.

The role is a mix of order fulfillment, light product production, inventory organization, and general logistical support. Some days will involve packing and shipping orders, while others might include preparing products for retail, assembling packaging, running production machines, organizing inventory, or general studio upkeep.

We're a small, growing business, so no two days are exactly alike! I'm looking for someone who enjoys working with their hands, has a good eye for detail, and is comfortable jumping between different tasks as needed.

**While we're initially hiring for a general studio assistant, we're hoping to find someone who can grow with us.** Render is entering an exciting new chapter of growth, and we'd love to find a long-term team member whose interests, experience, and individual strengths could eventually contribute to the business in a more meaningful way.

Render Goods is a woman-owned, Chicago-based housewares studio creating thoughtfully designed everyday essentials from recycled, biodegradable, and otherwise responsibly sourced materials.

Our collection includes colorful dish towels made from recycled plastic bottles, Swedish dishcloths, washcloths, and natural-fiber cleaning brushes. We sell through independent retailers, online, and at markets and events throughout the country.

Our Chicago studio serves as the home base for product development, light manufacturing, inventory, and fulfillment.

* Assist with larger wholesale orders and seasonal shipping volume.

**Product Finishing & Light Production**

* Inspect finished products for quality and presentation.
* Fold, bundle, package, and prepare products for retail and wholesale distribution.
* Assist with simple production and finishing tasks as needed.
* Help maintain consistency and quality across finished products.

**Studio Organization & Logistics**

* Receive deliveries, unpack shipments, and organize incoming inventory.
* Restock supplies and maintain an organized workspace.

* Assist with inventory counts and general stock organization.
* Help with miscellaneous studio projects and daily operational tasks.

**Events & Special Projects**

* Help prepare displays, merchandise, and supplies for upcoming events.
* Occasionally provide on-site assistance at larger Chicago markets and trade shows.
* Assist with new product development, samples, and creative projects as opportunities arise.

Requirements

* Reliable, punctual, organized, and detail-oriented.
* Comfortable working independently and following instructions.
* Good time management skills and ability to prioritize tasks.
* Strong attention to detail, particularly with packaging and order accuracy.
* Comfortable performing repetitive, hands-on tasks.
* Ability to lift and carry up to 40 lbs.
* Willingness to learn new processes and take initiative.
* Comfortable working directly with the founder in a small studio environment.
* Previous shipping, fulfillment, retail, or production experience is a plus, but not required.
